**Yes, Mondays have the highest stop count, but the lead comes mostly from one day.**

September 2026 weekday profile (all three shifts, 22 production days):

| Weekday | Days | Stops/day | Minutes/day | Minutes/stop |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mon | 4 | **33.3** | 54.0 | 1.62 |
| Fri | 4 | 27.8 | 46.5 | 1.68 |
| Wed | 5 | 27.4 | 40.6 | 1.48 |
| Tue | 5 | 27.2 | 41.7 | 1.53 |
| Thu | 4 | 25.0 | 165.3 | 6.61 |

- **Monday stops:** 7 Sep had 46 stops, 14 Sep had 28, 21 Sep had 27, and 28 Sep had 32. Without 7 Sep, the Monday average is about 29 stops, close to the other weekdays.
- **Monday stop length:** Monday stops are about the same length as other days (1.62 min), so the difference is in how many stops occur, not how long they last.
- **Thursday is the real downtime problem:** Thursdays have the fewest stops but about 165 minutes of downtime per day, roughly four times any other weekday. The cause is long stops (about 6.6 min each), not frequency. 3 Sep and 10 Sep were the worst days, and 17 and 24 Sep were similar.

For 14 Sep specifically, Monday had 28 stops and 46 minutes of downtime (3.2%), which is typical rather than elevated.
